title: Reducing Neuroinflammation and Risk of Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer’s Disease by Reducing Dietary Lipopolysaccharides, Arachidonic Acid, and Advanced Glycation End Products
content: Levels of lipopolysaccharide (LPS), arachidonic acid (AA), and advanced glycation end products (AGEs) are higher in the brain of subjects affected by cognitive impairment and Alzheimer’s disease(AD), compared to a healthy brain. Inflammatory cytokines, triggered by LPS and AGEs in food, can enter the brain via active transport and induce microglial activation, inflammation, and oxidative damage. AA can elicit neuroinflammation by increasing leukotriene-A4 and prostaglandin-E2 production. Increased levels of neuroinflammation are associated with poorer cognition in AD. A dietary reduction of LPS, AA, and AGEs could reduce risk and slow progression of cognitive impairment and AD by reducing neuroinflammation, through multiple mechanisms. The avoidance of foods that are highest in LPS, AGEs, and AA (dairy products, pork, poultry, beef, and seafood) and the emphasis on foods lowest in LPS, AGEs, and AA (fruits, vegetables, boiled whole grains, beans, raw nuts, and seeds) can reduce neuroinflammation and risk of cognitive impairment and AD. Reduction of chronic neuroinflammation with dietary changes may represent a novel approach to treatment of AD and cognitive decline.
